n4.title: feat(github): read the tracker with a Haiku scout, add findings to open issues
n4.body:
The `kalinichenko:github` skill now hands the reading of a large tracker to a Haiku subagent, adds a finding to an open issue on the same code before it files a new one, and checks every open bug and debt issue in the same area when an issue is taken into work, so one PR can close them with the task.

## What changes

- **New file `skills/github/scout.md`.** It is the whole instruction for a read-only scout. The scout reads every open title, searches issues and PRs by every file, symbol and on-screen word it gets, reads the candidates' bodies and the paginated timeline, and returns only the candidates in fixed groups. It gives no advice. In Claude Code the main agent sends it with one `Agent` call, `model: "haiku"`, and a four-line prompt from the new *The scout* section. In Codex the agent runs `scout.md` itself.
- **Only for a tracker of 30 open issues or more.** `gh issue list --state open --limit 30 --json number --jq length` prints `30` from that size. Below it, the agent runs `scout.md` itself, because a subagent's start costs more than the reading.
- **The scout reads, the main agent acts.** Every close, edit, comment and new issue stays with the main agent, and it reads each issue in full before it acts on it. The scout's report replaces the main agent's own search of the tracker. It searches only for a name the scout did not get.
- **Add to an open issue before you open a new one.** A finding goes into a host: an open issue whose fix changes the same code, or that decides something about the same function, and that nobody works on (no other assignee, no linked branch, no open PR). The agent adds a section to its body, keeps the old text, changes the title to name both problems, adds the label if it is missing, and leaves a one-line comment, because a body edit notifies nobody. A finding that is already filed, or that a closed issue or a merged PR already settles, is not filed. A new issue is filed only when there is no free host.
- **Check every open bug and debt issue in the same area first**, whatever the task is, a feature too. Bug and debt are the labels `bug` and `debt`, or the repository's own names for them. Each ends in one of four ways: already gone (close it with the evidence), the change removes it (a bug's test joins the PR, and it closes with it), it rides along, or it stays open. To ride along it passes the four existing tests, with *Same file* widened to the same area: a file of the screen, window or command the task changes. An issue the change removes does not count toward the ride-along total. In the take-in job, the scout reads the body of every open bug and debt issue, so one that names none of the task's files still shows up.
- **The timeline command** moves from `SKILL.md` into `scout.md`, with its `--paginate` note.
- **`rules.md` and `README.md`** describe the new filing order and the scout.

## Why

Reading the tracker is long and needs no knowledge of the task. On a tracker with 102 open issues it means about 4,000 tokens of titles, several search outputs and up to 30,000 tokens of bodies, and all of it stays in the main model's context to the end of the task. Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 / $0.50 per MTok against Opus 5.5's $4 / $20.

The tracker also grows faster than it closes. Two issues on one piece of code end up as two PRs that edit the same lines.

## Tested

These are dry runs on a private test tracker (102 open issues): read commands ran, and every write command was printed, not run. Nothing was written to that repository.

| Scenario | Before (current skill, Opus) | After (new skill, Opus + Haiku scout) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A finding with a free host on the same code (runner log lines carry no time, host #183) | — | Added to #183: section, new title, one-line comment. No new issue |
| A finding that a merged PR already settles (`KeepAlive` loop, PR #186) | Found it after 15 calls of its own. Its fallback was a new issue `Related to #183` | The scout returned it under **Already decided** |
| `#179` taken into work | 6 bugs in the area listed only because the test prompt asked for them | All 6 checked with a verdict each, with no prompt for it; #125 found by its own search for `window.ts` |
| Main agent repeats the scout's search | — | First run: 11 own searches. After the line "Its report is your search of the tracker": 0 |
| Debt in the same area as `#179` (the scout alone) | — | First run: none found. After every open bug and debt body became a candidate: #290, whose body lists the sheet among the windows that read the cache |

One more dry run on this repository (3 open issues), with a finding on `rules.md:85`: the count printed `3`, the agent ran `scout.md` itself with no subagent, and it added the finding to #7, which changes the same paragraph.

Main agent's tokens and tool calls:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Filing | ~83k / 15 | ~78k / 18, then ~68k / 14 after the fix above |
| Take-in `#179` | ~104k / 26 | ~97k / 28 (before the fix above) |

The scout itself took 4–11 calls, ~50–70k Haiku tokens and about one minute per run. With the files it got, it found every bug in the area that the Opus run found. It missed #125, because `window.ts` was not in its prompt. The skill tells the main agent to search such names itself, and in the test it did.

Two scout runs gave advice or a wrong shape at the end. The *Return* section now states the output as a recipe, and the later runs kept to it. Two runs skipped the long body of PR #292; read in parts of 4,000 characters, it was read.

`make check` passes.

## Review

Two read-only reviews ran on the branch: one on Fable, one on Codex. They gave 26 findings; 3 came from both. Each was checked against the files and the installed `gh` before a fix.

Fixed:

- **A host's open PR was never read.** The host test asks for "no open PR", but the scout read no source for it. It now reads `closedByPullRequestsReferences` (both reviews).
- **The base prompt told the scout to load the skill**, which `scout.md` forbids. `scout.md` now says that rule is for agents that write (both reviews).
- **A bug could close as already gone on one passing run**, or on a code reading with no reproduction. It now needs a commit that removed its cause and a passing reproduction; a bug with no reproduction, or one that shows only sometimes, stays open (both reviews).
- **Searches stopped at 30 hits**, the `gh` default. They now use `--limit 500` and run again past it (Codex).
- **A closed, completed issue with the same report suppressed a regression.** A new group, **Fixed before**, leads to a new issue that starts `Regression of #12` (Codex).
- **A long PR body was cut with no rule to read the rest.** The scout now reads every PR body to its end, in parts of 4,000 characters, and lists every body it read only in part (Codex). A first version left the rest to the scout's judgment, and one run then missed the decision in PR #186.
- **A merged PR found by name, not in the timeline, had no group.** **Linked** is now **Linked, open work and history** (Codex).
- **`gh issue develop` was forbidden and required.** `--list` is now allowed by name (Codex).
- **The take-in scout never read the issue in hand** (Fable).
- **"Keep the text that was there" gave no command**, and `gh issue edit --body` replaces the whole body. The skill now gives `--body-file` with the old body (Fable).
- **Run by the main agent, `scout.md`'s *Return* read as "end your turn".** The skill now says which parts apply (Fable).
- **A busy host would have its body edited** through *Filing one next to an existing issue*. It now gets only a one-line comment (Fable).
- Smaller ones: how to learn your own login, one group per finding, a `quote:` line, two example `Job:` lines, the worktree order, one `gh pr view` call, the title that "names every problem", and the prose that broke the base prompt's short-sentence rule, in `SKILL.md`, `scout.md` and `README.md` (Fable, Codex).

Not fixed:

- **"Tests of the issues the change removes bypass the size cap"** (Codex). These issues are fixed by the task's own code, so they cannot be dropped, and a bug's test is required by `rules.md`. The cap is for optional ride-alongs. The text now gives this reason.
- **A host had no size limit** (Fable). This was a decision for the owner: a host now takes at most two added findings. Each one starts `## Also: <the problem>`, and the scout counts those headings with one `jq` expression, so the count needs no judgment. The third finding files a new issue, `Related to` the host.

After the fixes, the Haiku scout ran again on both cases. Filing: host #183, `status: free`, confirmed against its empty `closedByPullRequestsReferences`. Take-in `#179`: all 7 bugs and debt issues in the area, #271 included, and 8 entries of history, such as #250 and PR #259, an earlier fix on the same `holdWindow` path.

### Rounds two and three

Two more rounds ran on the same two models. Round two gave 22 findings (1 high), round three 18, 17 of them distinct (none high); each was checked against the files before a fix. Every one was fixed, in `476f3c4` and the commit after it. The main ones:

- **An issue with `## Also:` sections closed on one problem's verdict.** Each problem now gets its own verdict; a change that fixes only some writes `Part of #15`, and *Finishing* adds `Done in #<PR>.` under each one fixed.
- **The two-finding cap read a count taken before the run wrote anything.** The agent counts the headings afresh, with the findings it added in the same run.
- **Someone else's work could be closed or absorbed.** The take-in check reads `closedByPullRequestsReferences` before the worktree is made; a duplicate, a ride-along or a bug with a `status:` other than `free` gets no verdict; a host's timeline is read for open PRs, and `status:` lists every state that applies.
- **The base prompt and `scout.md` disagreed.** `rules.md` now says a read-only scout does not load the skill and files nothing.
- **A behaviour kept on purpose could be filed as a regression.** **Already decided** now comes before **Fixed before**, and **Fixed before** needs the pull request that fixed it.
- **The scout missed what lives in comments, closed duplicates and open PRs during filing.** It reads comments, follows a duplicate to its survivor with a read-only GraphQL `duplicateOf` query (`gh issue view` has no such field), and returns a new **Open work** group.
- Smaller ones: the long forms `--field` and `--raw-field` in the `gh api` ban, GitHub's 1,000-result search ceiling, `mktemp` for the body file, five filing groups under each `Finding n:` line, and the prose.

## Limits

- **Main-model savings are modest on this tracker: 7–18 %.** The main agent still reads the code and the issues it acts on. The gain grows with the tracker, because the title list stays with the scout.
- **Codex gets no savings.** A Codex plugin cannot ship agents: its manifest has no `agents` field (`codex-rs/plugin/src/manifest.rs`). Codex runs `scout.md` itself. Its `spawn_agent` takes a `model`, so a smaller model is possible later.
- **A host takes at most two added findings.** The limit is a first value, to raise once real hosts show how big one PR can get.
- **The same area is a looser test than the same file.** For a bug or debt issue, a file of the same screen, window or command counts. The size cap on ride-alongs still holds, so the PR stays named for its task.
- **The take-in scout reads every open bug and debt body.** On a private test tracker that was 39 bodies, which the scout cut short on its own. A long body can hide a mention past the cut.

## Also fixed

Not part of the task:

- Rewrapped an over-long line in `rules.md` (the list of what the skill carries) and one in `SKILL.md` (the cross-repository guard).

## Follow-ups

More read-heavy steps that could go to a Haiku subagent the same way:

- #5 — the scout checks `path:line` citations, at take-in and at *Finishing*. Depends on this PR.
- #6 — the payload count before a bug fix (`rules.md`).
- #7 — the docs sweep for *Docs move with the change* (`rules.md`).

The steps with one correct result — collecting, counting, writing — move to scripts in #8.

n5.title: The Haiku scout does not check path:line citations: the main model reads every cited file itself
n5.body:
The main model checks every `path:line` citation in an issue by hand. This is mechanical, read-heavy work that the Haiku scout from #4 could do.

**Where.** Two steps of `skills/github/SKILL.md` (line numbers on the branch of #9):

- `:285`, taking an issue into work: check the issue's own `path:line` citations against the current tree, and correct them.
- `:352`, *Finishing*: update every sibling issue whose text the change just falsified.

**How it shows.** In #4's dry run of taking #179 of a private test tracker into work, the main model read the issue's citations and the cited files itself. It found a stale line in #197 (`sheets.ts` listens for `render-process-gone` only on a sheet, moved to `window.ts:284` since #292) and in #125 (`window.ts:179-180`, now `:205-206`). Each check is "read the issue, open the file, find the symbol, compare". The answer is one line per citation.

**What to do.** Add a third job, `citations`, to `skills/github/scout.md`:

- Input: the issue numbers and the tree to check against. For take-in, the issue in hand and the default branch. For *Finishing*, the open issues that name a file in `git diff --name-only origin/<default>...HEAD`, and the worktree.
- Output, one line per citation: holds, moved to `<path:line>`, or gone.
- The main model edits the issue bodies and leaves the comments, as now.

**Test.** Dry run on a private test tracker, take-in `#179`: the scout must report the two stale citations above, and the main model must not open the cited files for a citation the scout says holds.

**Why not in #4.** #4 reads the tracker only. This reads the code too, and needs its own test. It depends on #4: `scout.md` comes from there.


Related to #8: a script can print the cited lines, and the scout compares them. Since #9 the scout runs no command but `collect.sh bodies`: a `citations` job reads the cited files with its file tool, or gets the lines from such a script.

n6.title: The payload count before a bug fix runs on the main model, not on a Haiku subagent
n6.body:
The base prompt asks the agent to count real payloads before it believes a bug report. The main model reads the whole sample itself, and the answer is one number and a few examples. A Haiku subagent could do the reading.

**Where.** `rules.md:26`, in *A bug fix ships with its test*: "pull a sample of real payloads and say how many carry the shape". The measured case in the next paragraph read 100 bodies to get "0 of 100".

**What to do.** In Claude Code, give the counting to one `Agent` call with `model: "haiku"`, as #4 does for the tracker:

- Input: the source of the payloads, the sample size, and the shape to look for.
- Output: the count, the ids of the payloads that carry the shape, and one or two of them recorded verbatim — whitespace and all — for the test.
- The main model checks the shape on the returned examples, decides whether the fix needs to exist, and writes the test from a recorded payload. In Codex, the agent counts itself.

**Limit.** `rules.md` goes into every session and every subagent through `hooks/rules.sh`, and `tests/rules_test.sh` caps it at 10,000 characters. It is 8,133 on the branch of #9. The addition has room for one or two sentences; a longer recipe belongs in a skill.

**Test.** A bug-fix task with a payload source and a hand-written report. Before: the main model reads the sample itself. After: it sends the subagent, and the count matches a count the main model makes on the same sample.

**Why not in #4.** #4 is about the GitHub skill. This changes the base prompt, which every session loads.

Related to #4.

n7.title: The docs sweep for 'Docs move with the change' runs on the main model, not on a Haiku subagent
n7.body:
The base prompt asks the agent to name the docs a change made false. Finding them means reading the repository's docs on the main model, and the answer is a short list of `file:line`. A Haiku subagent could do the reading.

**Where.** `rules.md:81-91`, *Docs move with the change*: "Before finishing, name the docs the change touched, or say 'docs impact: none' with a one-line why." The candidates are the README, the project's instruction file, API docs and ADRs.

**What to do.** In Claude Code, give the sweep to one `Agent` call with `model: "haiku"`:

- Input: what the change alters — the behaviour, the names, the commands, the install steps — and the changed files.
- Output: one line per passage that is now false: `file:line`, the sentence, and why it no longer holds. Or "none", with the files it read.
- The main model edits the docs and names them in its report, as now. In Codex, the agent sweeps itself.

Claude Code's built-in `Explore` agent is read-only and may fit as the `subagent_type`. Check its default model before relying on it.

**Limit.** The same as for the payload count: `rules.md` is capped at 10,000 characters by `tests/rules_test.sh` and is 8,133 on the branch of #9. One or two sentences fit.

**Test.** A change that renames a command which the README and an instruction file both mention. Before: the main model greps and reads the docs itself. After: the subagent returns both passages, and the main model edits them without its own sweep.

**Why not in #4.** #4 is about the GitHub skill. This changes the base prompt.

Related to #4.

n8.title: The github skill describes its deterministic steps in prose: collecting, counting and writing are not scripts
n8.body:
The github skill and `scout.md` describe in prose many steps that have one correct result: commands, limits, pagination, counts and write sequences. The agent must follow each of these rules by hand, and a small model follows them worst.

**How it shows.** Three review rounds on #4 found many gaps of this kind: the `gh` default limit of 30, a PR body cut after its first part, `--field` missing from the write ban, GitHub's 1,000-result search ceiling, `mktemp` for the body file, `duplicateOf`, and the `## Also:` count taken before the run wrote anything. The Haiku scout skipped long PR bodies: #292 in two runs, #186 in one. A script does these steps the same way each time, and a test can prove it. A rule in prose cannot.

**Where.** Line numbers on `main`, after #4. About 1,250 of the 5,134 words in `skills/github/SKILL.md` and `skills/github/scout.md` describe such steps:

| Script | Replaces | Words now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/collect.sh` | *Read*, `scout.md:26-82`: every open title, the searches by name with `--limit 500` and the 1,000 ceiling, bodies and comments, `gh issue develop --list`, `closedByPullRequestsReferences`, the timeline with `--paginate`, `duplicateOf`, PR bodies in parts of 4,000 characters. The write ban, `scout.md:3-16` | ~660 |
| the same | `status:` and `also:`, `scout.md:117-121` and `:164-167` | ~85 |
| `scripts/add-finding.sh <n> <section-file> <title> [label]` | The host checks and the four steps that add a finding, `SKILL.md:158-177` | ~220 |
| `scripts/worktree.sh <n> <branch>` | `SKILL.md:244-270`: `develop --list`, `git worktree list`, `--worktree` and the path for gh older than 2.99, `info/exclude`, the check for a session already in a worktree | ~230 |
| `scripts/take-in-check.sh <n or URL>` | `SKILL.md:207-212`: closed, assigned to someone else, closed by someone else's open PR, or from another repository | ~60 |

**What stays with the model.** A title that names the same behaviour in other words. The groups. The verdicts: already gone, the change removes it, the four ride-along tests. The text of a section, a title and a branch name.

**What to do.**

- `collect.sh` writes everything to one file and prints its path and size. It works in two steps. First: every open title, the hits of each search, and the bodies, comments, `status:` and `also:` of the hits; for take-in, also of every open bug and debt issue. The bug and debt label names are an argument. Then the model picks candidates from the titles, and `collect.sh bodies <n>...` adds their bodies.
- The scout runs only `collect.sh` and reads its file. The write ban becomes that one rule.
- `add-finding.sh` reads `status:` and counts `## Also:` again just before it writes. It refuses a busy host and a full one.
- A script that writes takes `DRY_RUN=1`: it prints its write commands and runs none. The dry runs on a private test tracker need this.
- The scripts need only `bash` and `gh`: `gh --jq`, not `jq`. The skill calls them as `bash <skill directory>/scripts/<name>.sh`, because a plugin packager can drop the executable bit.
- The subagent is sent by the size of the file, not by the count of open issues. The main agent reads a small file itself; a large one goes to the subagent. The subagent keeps the main agent's context small, whatever its model. Haiku keeps its price low. Measure the size limit in the dry runs.

**Test.**

- `tests/github_scripts_test.sh`, with a fake `gh` first on `PATH`: `status:` for an assignee, a linked branch and an open PR; the `also:` count; `add-finding.sh` refuses a full host and a busy one; `DRY_RUN=1` runs no write. Add it to `make check`.
- The dry runs from #4 on a private test tracker. Filing: host #183, and PR #186 under **Already decided**. Take-in `#179`: all 7 bug and debt issues in the area, #290 included. Count the scout's calls. Give the same file to Haiku and to the main agent's model, and compare their groups.

**Why not in #4.** #4 passed three review rounds as it is. This changes how the scout reads, and needs its own tests.

Related to #5: its `citations` job can use a script that prints the cited lines, and the model compares them. Depends on #4: `scout.md` comes from there.

n9.title: feat(github): move the skill's steps with one correct result into scripts
n9.body:
The `kalinichenko:github` skill now runs its steps with one correct result as scripts. Four bash scripts read the tracker, check an issue before it is taken, add a finding to a host, and set up the worktree. A test proves each guard, which a rule in prose cannot do. The model keeps the choices: the candidates by meaning, the groups, the verdicts, and the text of a section, a title and a branch name.

Closes #8.

## What changes

- **`collect.sh`** reads the tracker into one file, and prints its path and size.
  - It writes every open title, and the hits of a search for each name, open and closed. A path is searched by its base name too.
  - It writes the body, the comments, `status:` and `also:` of every open hit. For take-in, it also writes the issue, its timeline with the body of each item, and every open issue with one of the bug and debt labels that the agent gives.
  - `collect.sh bodies <file> <n>...` adds the closed hits and the title candidates that the reader picks. A number already in the file gets no second entry. An issue closed as a duplicate brings the issue it duplicates.
  - One GraphQL query reads 20 issues with all of this: assignees, linked branches, closing PRs, the timeline, comments and `duplicateOf`. Searches use `--limit 1000`, and the file says when one reaches GitHub's 1,000-hit ceiling. PR bodies are written whole.
- **The scout reads that file and runs only `collect.sh bodies`.** The write ban in `scout.md` becomes that one rule. `scout.md` gets a section on the file's format. Its groups and its *Return* stay.
- **The size of the file decides who reads it**, not the count of open issues. In Claude Code a file of 20 KB or more goes to a Haiku scout. A smaller file, and every file in Codex, the main agent reads with `scout.md`.
- **`add-finding.sh <n> <section-file> <title> [label]`** reads `status:` and `also:` again just before it writes. It refuses a busy host, a full one and a closed one, and then writes nothing. Otherwise it sets the body, the title and the label in one edit, and leaves the one-line comment.
- **`take-in-check.sh <n or URL>`** prints `take #91`, or each reason to wait or stop: closed, assigned to someone else, closed by someone else's open PR, or in another repository.
- **`worktree.sh <n> <branch>`** reuses a linked branch, works where a branch is already checked out, stays in a session's own worktree, falls back for gh older than 2.99, and adds `.claude/worktrees/` to `info/exclude`. It prints the path to work in.
- **`DRY_RUN=1`** on the two scripts that write prints the write commands and runs none. `GH_REPO` points the `gh` calls at another repository.
- The skill calls the scripts as `bash <dir>/scripts/<name>.sh`. They run on bash 3.2, the `/bin/bash` of macOS, and filter only with `gh --jq`, not `jq`.
- `README.md` and `rules.md` describe the scripts and the new limit.

## Two changes to the plan in #8

- **Closed hits get no body in the first file.** #8 asked for the bodies of all hits. On a private test tracker take-in #179 that gave 388 KB and 83 entries. 300 KB of it were closed issues and merged PRs that the word `sheet` found. With the open hits, the timeline, and the bugs and debt only, the file is 107 KB and 34 entries. The reader picks closed hits by title and adds them with `bodies`, as #8 planned for title candidates.
- **The limit is 20 KB.** The scout's reports measured 3–7 KB. A main agent that reads the file itself also reads the bodies it adds: the filing file grew from 24.6 KB to 78 KB in the first run. So from about 20 KB, the scout costs the main agent less. The first runs used 50 KB; the table shows both.

## Tested

`make check` passes. It now runs `tests/github_scripts_test.sh`: a fake `gh` first on `PATH` answers from GraphQL payloads recorded on this repository's #5, each case changed with `jq`. a private test tracker is private, so none of its payloads is in this repository. The cases:

- `status:` for an assignee, a linked branch, an open PR that closes the issue and one in its timeline; a PR from another repository does not count.
- `also:` counts only `## Also:` headings.
- `add-finding.sh` refuses a busy host, a full one and a closed one, and writes nothing. The new body is the old one and the section.
- `DRY_RUN=1` runs no write in `add-finding.sh` and `worktree.sh`.
- `bodies` skips a number already in the file.
- `take-in-check.sh` gives each reason; `worktree.sh` reuses a linked branch.

Each guard was broken in turn, and the test failed each time.

Dry runs on a private test tracker (103 open issues): the reads ran, and every write was printed, not run.

| Run | Reader | File | Calls | Tokens | Time | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Filing: runner log lines carry no time; the `KeepAlive` loop | Opus main agent, 50 KB limit | 24.6 KB, 78 KB after `bodies` | 20 | 114k | 4 min | Host #183; PR #186 under **Already decided** |
| The same, after the fixes below | Haiku scout, 20 KB limit | 24.5 KB, 56 KB after `bodies` | 4 | 74k | 49 s | Host #183; PR #186 under **Already decided**. The main agent got a 3 KB report |
| Take-in #179 | Haiku scout | 107 KB | 5 | 110k | 75 s | 6 bugs and debt, #290 included. Left out the three timeline PRs |
| The same file | Opus | 107 KB | 7 | 115k | 131 s | 4 bugs and debt, neighbour #19, 7 history entries |
| Take-in #179, after the fixes below | Haiku scout | 107 KB, 148 KB after `bodies` | 14 | 117k | 137 s | 7 bugs and debt, #290 included; neighbours #19 and #304; 11 history entries, PRs #185, #244 and #292 included |

Haiku and Opus on the same file: both found #181, #197, #290 and #305. Haiku also kept #196, #302 and #164, and marked them as weak, as `scout.md` asks. Only Haiku found #250 and PR #259, an earlier fix on the same `holdWindow` path.

In #4's runs the scout skipped the long bodies of PR #292 and PR #186. Both are now in the file whole, and Haiku quoted from both.

`collect.sh` took 16–21 s per run. `add-finding.sh` in dry run printed the edit and the comment for #183; the body file kept the old text and added the section at its end.

### Fixed after the first dry runs

- The Haiku scout left the timeline PRs out. `scout.md` now puts every item of `== Its timeline` in **Linked, open work and history**.
- The examples in `SKILL.md` and `scout.md` used the test bed's paths and issue numbers, #183 and #186 among them, so they told a dry run the answer. They are neutral now.
- The limit went from 50 KB to 20 KB.
- `bodies` wrote a second entry for a number already in the file. It skips it now.
- `add-finding.sh` left its body file in `$TMPDIR`. It deletes it after a real run, and keeps it in a dry run.
- The file's first line listed the names without quotes, so `runner log` read as two names. The names are now only in the `== Search:` lines.

Not changed: the Haiku scout misread its file twice. It said a part had no end line, and that #228 had no entry. The script wrote both.

## Review

`/code-review xhigh` gave 15 findings. I checked each against the code or ran it. Fixed in `cc9a3b0`, each with a test that failed first:

- **A failed GraphQL query was ignored.** Bash does not stop inside `$(...)`, and `each` returned the status of its last `shift`. A failed `duplicateOf` or timeline query gave a file with parts missing and exit 0. `each` now returns gh's failure, and the script stops.
- **Your own PR made an issue someone else's work.** #5 showed `status: PR #9`, and PR #9 is this one; it only names #5. So #5 could not take a finding. `status:` now names each PR's author and you as `you`. A new `taken:` line is computed from the logins, not from the text, and `add-finding.sh` reads it. `SKILL.md` defines *someone else's work* once.
- **`bodies` wrote its heading before it fetched.** A failed query left a broken part in the file. It now writes only after every query succeeds.
- **A duplicate brought back an entry that the file already held**, the issue in hand too. `entries` now skips every number with an entry in the file.
- **A part with no entries had no `== end` line.** It now ends with `== end: 0 entries`.
- **Limits that cut with no notice.** Closing PRs: 100, not 10, so ten closed attempts cannot hide an open one. The open titles: a note at 1,000.
- **Issue numbers were not checked** in `status` and `take-in`: `#5` broke the query, and a PR number crashed jq. Now `#5` works, and a PR is refused as a host.
- **`usage` left out the take-in line.**
- **`worktree.sh` took the first linked branch**, even when the branch it was given was linked too.
- **Filing and take-in had no test.** Filing now runs on recorded lists: the open hits get bodies, merged PRs do not, and a search with no open hits ends with `== end: 0 entries`.
- **The test left a body file in `$TMPDIR`.** It now keeps its files in its own directory.

Changed in the docs only:

- **Two `add-finding.sh` runs on one host at once can lose a section.** `SKILL.md` now says to run it for one host at a time. There is no lock: GitHub has no compare-and-set for an issue body, and a local lock covers one machine only.

Not fixed:

- **Repeated reads.** Take-in reads the issue twice, `duplicateOf` takes one more query per 20 issues, and `add-finding.sh` reads the body twice. One read would need the jq output split in bash. That costs more code to save about a second.
- **One rule for `take-in-check.sh` and `status:`.** The two rules differ on purpose. Take-in waits only for an assignee or a closing PR by someone else, as `SKILL.md` has said since #4. With `status:`'s rule, take-in would also wait for linked branches. GitHub does not say whose a branch is, so the agent would wait on its own branch.

## Limits

- **Fewer words than #8 expected.** `SKILL.md` and `scout.md` went from 5,134 to 4,896 words, not about 1,250 fewer. The calls of the scripts and the section on the file's format take words too.
- **The 20 KB limit was measured on two trackers only.** It is a first value, like the two-finding cap from #4.
- **Haiku reads a 107 KB file in 5–14 calls and about 115k tokens.** It keeps doubtful candidates, as asked, and it misread its file twice.
- **An entry holds the newest 100 timeline references and the first 100 comments.** It says when an issue has more comments.
- **A search past 1,000 hits is not split by state.** The file says that the list can be cut.
- **`worktree.sh` ran in this repository and in a temporary one only.** This session cannot run `git` in another checkout.

## Also fixed

Not part of the task:

- The *Return* example in `scout.md` named the second finding's file under the first finding.

## Issues

- #5 cites two lines of `SKILL.md` that this change moves. Its body now cites them where this branch has them, and says how a `citations` job reads the code now that the scout runs only `collect.sh bodies`.
- #6 and #7 give the size of `rules.md`. This change makes it 8,133 characters, and their bodies now say so.

n10.title: The github skill loads all of SKILL.md for a commit message: split it into files by moment
n10.body:
The `kalinichenko:github` skill keeps every moment in one `SKILL.md`. Claude Code loads the whole file each time the skill is invoked, and `rules.md` invokes it before every `git commit` and every `gh` call. So the agent reads about 3,800 words to write a commit message, and it needs about 600 of them.

**Where.** `skills/github/SKILL.md` on the branch of #9: 382 lines, 3,789 words.

| Section | Words | Needed for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The table and the opening | ~350 | every moment |
| Commits | 244 | a commit |
| Pull requests | 236 | a PR, a merge |
| Scripts, Reading the tracker | 366 | take-in, filing |
| Filing an issue | 765 | a finding out of scope |
| An issue is a document too | 1,714 | `#91`: take-in, neighbours, *Finishing* |
| GitHub Actions | 112 | a workflow |

`scout.md` (1,107 words) already loads only when the agent reads it.

**How it shows.** A commit message or a PR loads all 3,789 words. Take-in alone is 45 % of them. Commits and PRs are probably the most frequent reasons to invoke the skill; this is not measured.

**What to do.** One skill, with a file for each moment:

- `SKILL.md`, about 1,000 words: the table, commits, PRs, merging and Actions. Each row of the table names the file to read before the first step.
- `take-in.md`: taking an issue into work, its duplicates, the worktree, the neighbours, *Finishing*.
- `filing.md`: findings out of scope, hosts, new issues, filing next to an existing issue.
- Reading the tracker (`collect.sh`, and who reads its file): take-in and filing both need it. It stays in `SKILL.md`, or it goes in a file of its own that both name.
- `scout.md` and `scripts/` stay as they are.

**Why not separate skills.**

- Take-in and filing share the scripts, the scout, and the rules for a host, `## Also:` and `status:`. Each skill has its own base directory, so the scripts would be copied, or reached through another skill's directory.
- One task often needs take-in, filing, a commit and a PR in turn. That is three or four skills to invoke.
- `rules.md` names one entry point, `kalinichenko:github`. More skills take more of its 10,000 characters; the branch of #9 uses 8,133.
- Each skill's description is in every session, and the descriptions compete for one request: a bare `#91` fits a take-in skill and the github skill.

**Risk.** The agent must open the right file at the right moment. The table must say it plainly, for example: "`#91` → read `take-in.md` before the first step".

**Test.**

- Count the words loaded for a commit message, before and after.
- Dry runs as in #4 and #9, on a private test tracker with `DRY_RUN=1`: take-in `#179` and filing. The agent reads `take-in.md` or `filing.md` before its first step, and the results match those of #9.
- A task that only commits: the agent reads `SKILL.md` and nothing else.

**Why not in #9.** #9 is named for #8 and passed its dry runs. This change moves text, and it needs dry runs of its own.

Depends on #9: it splits the `SKILL.md` that #9 changes. Related to #5: the two steps that #5 cites move to `take-in.md`.

source.title: The Haiku scout does not check path:line citations: the main model reads every cited file itself
